name: Plumber Website Sales Coach
offer: A fast, mobile-first website built to turn local searches into calls and booked plumbing jobs, with clear service pages, trust signals, and a simple quote request path.
goal: Diagnose why the plumber is not getting enough of the right calls, connect that problem to the website, and secure one specific next step such as a short website review or a tailored proposal.
buyer: Plumbing owner-operator or the person who handles the office and phone.
discovery: What is bringing you most of your jobs right now?
When someone searches for a plumber in your area, what do they find?
How many calls or booked jobs does your website bring in a typical month?
What happens when someone calls after hours or while your team is on a job?
Which jobs are most profitable for you, and which do you want more of?
What have you tried before to get more calls, and what happened?
Who else would be involved in a decision like this?
If the website brought more of the right jobs, what would that be worth to you?
pain_hypotheses: Word of mouth and referrals leave the pipeline uneven.
They get price shoppers or low-value jobs instead of the work they want.
The current site is slow or awkward to use on a phone.
Calls are missed after hours or while the team is on site.
The business looks less established than nearby competitors.
There is no obvious way to request a quote or book a job.
value_angles: More calls from people already searching for a plumber nearby.
Better-qualified jobs, not just more traffic.
A site that makes a small team look established and trustworthy.
Mobile-first service pages with a clear call or quote action.
Solid local SEO foundations without promising rankings.
Less time spent answering the same basic questions on the phone.

objections.move: Ask whether it brings in calls and when it was last updated. Do not attack the current site.

objections.when: they get enough work from word of mouth
objections.move: Ask about slow periods, after-hours calls, and the high-value jobs they would like more of.

objections.when: price, budget, or cost comes up
objections.move: Do not guess a number. Ask which jobs or outcomes matter most, then explain the next step is a scoped proposal.

objections.when: they say they are too busy
objections.move: Focus on a done-for-you process and the small amount of owner time needed. Do not add pressure.

objections.when: a friend, nephew, or another agency built the current site
objections.move: Respect the existing work. Ask what happens when it needs updates, tracking, or ongoing improvements.

objections.when: they say they do not need more work
objections.move: Shift from more leads to better jobs, stronger trust, and fewer time-wasting enquiries.

objections.when: they mention Google, SEO, or rankings
objections.move: Speak plainly about local visibility and conversion. Never promise a ranking or a lead count.

objections.when: they had a bad experience before
objections.move: Ask what went wrong and what would make this different. Diagnose before defending yourself.

objections.when: they ask you to send information
objections.move: Agree, confirm the one detail that matters most, and lock in a specific follow-up time.

objections.when: they say they are not interested
objections.move: Ask what would need to change for a website to matter, or ask permission for a low-pressure follow-up.

close: Ask for a short 15-minute website review.
Offer to send a tailored plan with scope and price after one final detail.
If timing is the issue, agree a specific follow-up date.
Ask who else should review the plan before a decision.
